label: Young And Cold Records
description: Four tracks of darkwave and goth, leaning synth, pop reissued through Young And Cold, the German label that has spent the last decade quietly mapping this exact corner. Sits comfortably next to the Selofan end of the roster.

title: The Acrobat
label: Dais Records
description: Dais reissues the Death Of Lovers LP, eight tracks of widescreen post, punk that has always sat closer to shoegaze haze than to gothic austerity. For anyone whose Nothing and Whirr shelves are already in order.

title: Mama Said
label: Virgin America (2)
description: Reissue of Kravitz's 1991 second album, fourteen tracks of soul, leaning rock that leaned harder into the heartbreak register than the debut. Virgin America back catalogue, for anyone who still files Are You Gonna Go My Way next to Bill Withers.

title: Cheek To Cheek
label: Streamline Records (3)
description: Streamline puts the Bennett/Gaga standards collaboration back on wax for Record Store Day, nineteen tracks of straight, down, the, middle big, band jazz vocal. More of a souvenir pressing than a discovery, but the duets still swing.

title: சூறாவளி "Cyclone"
label: Good Morning Tapes
description: Dechery turns up on Good Morning Tapes with a two, part mix drawn from Tamil film music, issued as a limited mixtape. Closer to a curatorial dispatch than a club tool, and very much in keeping with the label's slow, burn cassette catalogue.

title: Analog Fingerprints Vol. 0
label: Numbers.
description: Marco Passarani turns up on Numbers. with eight tracks of analog, rig electro and techno, the kind of hardware, led Roman science he has been refining since the Final Frontier days. For anyone keeping a Lory D shelf nearby.

title: Chainless
label: Young And Cold Records
description: Four tracks of coldwave on Young And Cold, the German label that has been quietly cataloguing this corner of post, punk for years. Test pressing on white label 12", shelve near Tearful Moon.

title: Madeleine
label: Knekelhuis
description: Twelve tracks of art, rock, folk and synth, pop bent into experimental shapes, landing on Knekelhuis where that kind of stylistic drift always finds a home. Sits comfortably alongside the label's Sissi Rada end of the catalogue.

title: State Of Grace
label: Hellcat Records
description: Boston street punk vets back on Hellcat for an eleven, track LP of working, class Oi! and melodic hardcore, pressed in limited reissue form. Shelve next to Dropkick Murphys if you need the obvious pointer.

title: Oda
label: Mondoj
description: Vic Bang's full, length for Mondoj sits in the abstract end of the label's catalogue, eight tracks of experimental electronics issued on limited LP. For listeners already keeping pace with the Mondoj run.

title: Move Your Body (Lee Foss & Micah Baxter Remix)
label: Helix Records (7)
description: Lee Foss and Micah Baxter take a pass at the Chicago house anthem, landing on Helix as a digital single. The kind of update built for current club rotation rather than the archive.

title: Cry Baby
label: Atlantic
description: Atlantic gives the 2015 Martinez debut an LP pressing, seventeen tracks of nursery, rhyme alt, pop wired into trap percussion and brittle synth, pop. A foundational document for the cohort that followed her into the charts.

title: पर्वत (The Mountain)
label: Kong (7)
description: Fifteen, track Gorillaz LP through their own Kong imprint, the genre map (Latin pop, Indo, pop, indie and alt, pop strands) suggesting Damon Albarn is again routing the cartoon band through whichever scenes have caught his ear. Business as usual, which has rarely meant predictable.

title: Bass Is The Space
label: Ilian Tape
description: re:ni links up with BiggaBush for a four, tracker on Ilian Tape, weighting the Zenker brothers' usual techno remit toward sound system dub and UK bass pressure. A 45 RPM 12" for the Pessimist crowd.

artist: Kassel Jaeger & Stephan Mathieu & Akira Rabelais
title: Zauberberg
label: Shelter Press
description: A reissue of the three, way Shelter Press session for processed field recordings and slowly decaying tone, two long pieces that sit closer to acousmatic composition than ambient. For anyone who wore through the original pressing or anything on Kesh.

artist: Nightmares On Wax Vs Adrian Sherwood
title: Flippin' Eck
label: Warp Records
description: George Evelyn handed over to Adrian Sherwood for a versioning job, which is about as logical a pairing as Warp has greenlit in a while. Two tracks of trip hop dragged through On, U Sound's mixing desk; shelve near Smith & Mighty.

title: Kinds
label: Warp Records
description: Kwes. heads to Warp with nine pieces of ambient leaning electronic, a quieter register than the pop production work he is better known for. Sits comfortably alongside the more song, shaped end of the label's roster.

title: PAN 003
label: Pan Records (24)
description: Four, track deep house compilation on Pan Records, the third in the catalogue and the kind of unhurried 12" you file alongside the steadier end of the Quintessentials roster.

title: Street Druid
label: AD 93
description: Eight tracks from the London saxophonist on AD 93, pulling his horn through dub techno haze, electroacoustic drift and a loose future, jazz pulse. Sits comfortably next to Beatrice Dillon for anyone working that side of the label.

title: All Things Might Spill
label: Shelter Press
description: Eight pieces of drone and contemporary ambient from Chantal Michelle, landing on Shelter Press where this kind of patient, slightly austere composition has long had a home. Sits comfortably alongside Félicia Atkinson on the shelf.

title: I Feel Alive
label: Musique TOPS
description: Eleven tracks of soft, focus indie pop from the Montreal group, repressed on their own Musique TOPS imprint. Their AM, radio touch and breezy songcraft remain the draw, file alongside Men I Trust.

title: Otonoma
label: Thrill Jockey
description: Hirano lands on Thrill Jockey with ten pieces of piano, leaning electroacoustic work, the kind of patient ambient and modern classical writing she has built across the last decade. For listeners who keep Hatakeyama and Ian William Craig within reach.

title: Stardust
label: Warp Records
description: Brown back on Warp with a fourteen, track set that, per the tags, leans further into electro and hyperpop than the rap purists will want. Closer in spirit to the Atrocity Exhibition lineage than to Quaranta, with the sugar dialled up.

title: It's Immaterial
label: Ghostly International
description: Ghostly reissues the Chris Stewart project's gauzy synth, pop on vinyl, eleven tracks of coldwave drift sung from somewhere behind the drum machine. For anyone whose Cure and New Order shelves keep wandering toward Sacred Bones.

title: Αν Είχαν Τ' Άστρα Δάκρυα
label: Heaven OST
description: A single tied to the Heaven OST imprint, sitting in the Greek folk lineage rather than anywhere club, adjacent. File alongside the more austere end of Mediterranean vocal records.

title: Ich Bin Meine Maschine - Remixed (30 Years Anniversary Edition)
label: Raster-Noton
description: Uwe Schmidt's Ich Bin Meine Maschine gets reworked for its 30th anniversary, four remixes pressed to 12" via Raster, Noton, the label that has long been Atom™'s natural home for his clinical, German, language techno conceptualism.

title: The Flicker
label: Ruined By Numbers
description: Two long, form drone pieces from the Mertens and Steenkiste pairing, issued in a limited edition on Ruined By Numbers. Patient, acoustic, leaning experimental work for anyone tracking the quieter edges of the Belgian minimalist circuit.

title: Masquerade
label: So Young Records
description: Ten tracks of guitar, led indie rock from the Irish five, piece on So Young, a label whose roster (Folly Group, English Teacher) tends to favour songwriting with some grit under the fingernails. Worth a listen if you've been keeping tabs on that scene.

title: And So It Is
label: Leaving Records
description: Eight tracks of spiritual and contemporary jazz from Aaron Shaw, arriving on Leaving Records in a limited LP pressing. Sits comfortably alongside the label's Carlos Niño orbit.

title: Blasé Saint
label: Sferic
description: Eight pieces of ambient for Sferic, the Manchester label whose roster has quietly defined a certain washed, room, tone strain of the genre. File alongside Loris S. Sarid or Ulla if you need bearings.

title: Chernobyl Gesture
label: Bearded Punk Records
description: Thirteen tracks of melodic pop punk from Brookhurst, landing on Belgium's Bearded Punk for the LP. Straight, ahead stuff for the Epitaph and Fat Wreck shelf, no apologies offered.

title: Nothing But Fixes
label: Modern Love
description: Four tracks of bass, grime and techno pressed at 45 for Modern Love, the Manchester label continuing its long flirtation with sound, system weight. Steel yourself for something closer to Rainy Miller's orbit than the label's ambient wing.

title: Rich EP
label: Lapsus Music
description: Four tracks of straightforward club house from Strieder for Lapsus, the Barcelona imprint that tends toward the deeper, dubbier end of the floor. Functional rather than showy.

title: I Wanna Be Your Dog Again
label: Them Hellas
description: Duckwrth in his looser, funk, leaning mode, a single sitting closer to the soul, pop side of his catalog than to straight rap. Self, released through Them Hellas.

title: Trying Times
label: Good Boy Records (6)
description: Blake on his own Good Boy imprint, leaning further into the ambient register that has shadowed his vocal records for years. Thirteen tracks, limited LP, more inward than the pop framing suggests.

title: Mastery Quantum Sound
label: Houndstooth
description: A twelve, track ambient compilation on Houndstooth, pressed in a limited LP run. The label has been quietly building this side of its catalogue for years, and the format here suggests something closer to a curated set than a sampler.

title: American Hunger (Lunch)
label: Vinyl Digital
description: One of three sequels to MF Grimm's notorious 60, track triple LP, twenty cuts of plainspoken, politically alert New York rap getting a Vinyl Digital pressing. For listeners who stuck with the original American Hunger across all three discs.

title: Πεπρωμένο Μου
label: Heaven OST
description: Stavros Siolas turns up on Heaven OST with a single that sits on the folk side of the label's catalogue rather than its club one. File alongside the more song, shaped corners of the roster.

title: Natural Selection
label: Pan (3)
description: Hecker returns to PAN with nine pieces of psychoacoustic abstraction, the kind of granular, room, warping computer music he has been building out for two decades. Difficult listening that rewards a good pair of speakers.

title: For Almost Ever
label: Scat Records (2)
description: Six tracks of Cleveland power, pop and punk from the Mice, returning via Scat, the label that has long looked after Robert Pollard adjacent Ohio guitar music. File next to Guided By Voices if you need a shelf.

title: ISS012
label: Ilian Tape
description: Four more tracks from the Zenker brothers' most reliable export, sticking to the breakbeat, and, techno braid he has been refining across the ISS series. Ilian Tape on Ilian Tape business.

title: Ultra Villain
label: NAFF
description: Fourteen tracks of leftfield pop from Maara on NAFF, leaning into trip hop drag and IDM detail without losing the song shapes underneath. A producer's record that still wants to be sung along to.

title: In The Red
label: Snappy Little Numbers
description: Denver pop, punk lifers back on Snappy Little Numbers with a one, sided 7", which tells you most of what you need to know about the intent. Melodic, fast, no B, side hedging.

title: Kansai Botanicals
label: Quiet Details
description: Scott Monteith takes his long, running dub project into Quiet Details territory, eight pieces threading field recordings through the kind of weighted, low, frequency haze he has worked in for two decades. Patient listening; shelve near Yagya.

title: Eeeeeeee
label: Short Span
description: Six tracks of dub techno from Picture on Short Span, cut across 33 and 45 for whatever reason the engineer decided. Functional rather than reverent, closer in spirit to Yagya than to the Basic Channel canon.

title: Love Letters To Ghosts
label: Young And Cold Records
description: Ten tracks of darkwave and post, punk from Casket Cassette, repressed on Young And Cold. Sits comfortably alongside the label's wider roster of cold synths and reverb, drenched guitars.

title: Don't Trust Mirrors
label: Warp Records
description: Ten pieces of prepared, piano composition from Moran on Warp, sitting where her modern classical work tends to settle, between Cage's lineage and the label's more pensive electronic roster. For anyone who kept returning to Ultraviolet.

title: Graze The Bell
label: Plancha
description: Bing & Ruth's pianist steps out solo on RVNG Intl., eight pieces of minimalist contemporary writing with a jazz tilt at the edges. Sits comfortably next to Kelly Moran on the same shelf.

title: Princess Of Power (Deluxe)
label: Queenie Records
description: Deluxe expansion of Marina's Princess Of Power on her own Queenie imprint, eighteen tracks of dance, pop and electro maximalism with the synth, pop scaffolding she has built a career on. For listeners who want the full pop architecture rather than the radio cut.

title: Voice
label: Smalltown Supersound
description: Eleven solo improvisations from the Ethiopian, Swedish vocalist, delivered without accompaniment and arriving on Smalltown Supersound. Extended, technique singing as the entire surface; closer to Maja Ratkje than to anything in the label's pop wing.

title: Banging On EP
label: Lapsus Music
description: Three tracks of functional, slightly cheeky tech house from Hotswing on Lapsus, aimed squarely at the floor rather than the headphones. File alongside the label's usual peak, time fare.

title: Through Global Frequency
label: 12th Isle
description: Banabila lands on 12th Isle with ten pieces stitching ambient, spoken word and shortwave, style sound poetry into something closer to radio, collage than song. Suits the label's archival, leaning cast, shelve near Pep Llopis or Áine O'Dwyer.

title: Home Is Everywhere and Nowhere at Once
label: Theory Therapy
description: Nine tracks of ambient, downtempo and dub bleed for Theory Therapy, the kind of low, lit, displaced atmospherics the label has been quietly building a catalogue around. Limited pressing; shelve near Topdown Dialectic.

title: Euphoria Bound
label: AD 93
description: Shackleton on AD 93 with ten tracks of the rolling, ritualistic bass, and, dub architecture he's been chiselling at for the better part of two decades. Limited LP for those still working through Skull Disco.

title: Naeem (Can’t You Hear Crying) (Live From La Prima Estate Festival, Lido di Camaiore, Italy. June 17 2023)
label: Jagjaguwar
description: A live capture of Naeem from a 2023 Italian festival set, released as a standalone single on Jagjaguwar. The arrangement loosens in the open air, leaning into the song's gospel pulse rather than the studio version's processed edges.

title: Heavy Mental
label: Producer Plug records
description: Geffen reissues the Wu, adjacent landmark across twenty tracks, Killah Priest's biblical, sprawling vision of conscious rap given another pressing. Still as dense and unhurried as anything from the GZA orbit.

title: I Did This To Myself
label: Brainfeeder
description: Three tracks pairing Stephen Bruner's bass, led falsetto pop with Lil Yachty's recent appetite for stranger production choices, landing on Brainfeeder where this kind of cross, wiring tends to live comfortably. Worth a look if Drunk still gets regular rotation.

title: RAMZTEK
label: ONO Records (3)
description: Ramzi shifts toward the dancefloor on RAMZTEK, seven tracks of leftfield tech house that keep the humid, off, kilter pulse of her FATi work intact. Closer to a club tool than her usual aquatic detours, but still recognisably hers.

title: Evolution
label: Plattenbau Ost
description: Ten tracks from Hagen Stoll and Rilla on Plattenbau Ost, sitting in the rap, meets, rock corner the German underground has long had a soft spot for. Closer to working, band record than studio construct.

title: Martyr
label: Young And Cold Records
description: Reissue and remaster of the Rosegarden Funeral Party LP through Young And Cold, the German imprint that has quietly become a clearing house for goth and coldwave revivalists. Eight tracks, full of the theatrical post, punk drama the band trade in.

title: The Chopping Block
label: Young And Cold Records
description: Six tracks of post, punk leaning into shoegaze haze, landing on Young And Cold in a limited 12". Goth, rock bones with the guitars pushed wide, for anyone whose shelf already holds Lebanon Hanover.

title: Been Undone (Full Moon Version)
label: Real World Records
description: Another Full Moon variant from the i/o cycle, Gabriel's long, running practice of issuing the same songs in different mixes through Real World. Downtempo and unhurried, for listeners who treat the alternate versions as the actual record.

title: Play Boy / Descarga Roger's
label: Vampi Soul
description: Vampi Soul digs up a split 45 pairing two obscure Latin sides, Los Playboys on the A and Los Roger's on the flip. The kind of one, and, done 7" the label has built its reputation reissuing.

title: Scrap Metal
label: Helix Records (4)
description: Twelve, track Helix compilation issued through Perris Records, the California outpost that has spent decades servicing collectors of late, eighties hard rock. Strictly for the leather, and, Marshall, stack faithful.

title: Play
label: Rhino Records (2)
description: Rhino's remastered reissue of the 1991 Squeeze record that landed them squarely in their post, imperial phase, Difford and Tilbrook still writing tighter pop songs than most of their alt, rock peers. Seventeen tracks across the LP edition.

title: Checking In
label: R & S Records
description: Two tracks of experimental techno from Viclan, landing on R & S as a digital, only check, in. Functional enough for the floor without quite settling there.

title: Vacancy
label: Interscope Records
description: Ari Lennox moves to Interscope for a fifteen-track R&B set pressed as a limited LP. Her Dreamville run already established the register, warm, conversational, unhurried; this one lands in the same neighborhood.

title: Chala (My Soul Is On A Loop)
label: Ninja Tune
description: Barry Can't Swim eases off the dancefloor for Ninja Tune, a downtempo single whose parenthetical title does most of the heavy lifting. Patient, melodic, and built for headphones rather than peak time.

artist: John Williams (4) = ジョン・ウィリアムズ
title: Harry Potter And The Prisoner Of Azkaban (Music From And Inspired By The Motion Picture) = ハリー・ポッターとアズカバンの囚人 [オリジナル・サウンドトラック]
label: Warner Sunset Records
description: Warner Sunset returns Williams' 2004 Azkaban score to physical format in a limited Japanese pressing, the entry in the franchise where the writing turns properly Prokofiev, shadowed and stops being children's music. 21 cues across the album.

title: Blade Runner
label: EastWest
description: EastWest reissues the score that more or less wrote the rulebook for cinematic synth ambient, twelve tracks of CS, 80 haze, noir saxophone and weather. Foundational listening for anyone tracking how film music drifted into the ambient canon.

title: Been Undone (Bright-Side Mix)
label: Real World Records
description: An alternate mix from Gabriel's own Real World, sitting at the polished end of his late, period catalogue rather than its stranger corners. One for listeners who've stayed with him past i/o.

title: I Love The Darkness Remixed
label: Wild Youth Digital
description: A two, track remix package from Der Würfler on Wild Youth Digital, working the title cut through a nu, disco lens. For the crate that still has room next to Mushrooms Project.

title: balança e paixão
label: Modern Love
description: Twelve tracks of experimental favela funk landing on Modern Love, a label more often associated with Mancunian gloom than Rio percussion. The collision is the point; expect the rhythm to be load, bearing and the edit work to be unkind.

title: Transfer
label: Other People
description: Two tracks of dub techno on Nicolas Jaar's Other People, pressed as a 45rpm 12". The label has been quietly drifting toward the format's slower, more eroded register; this fits.

title: Under the Influence
label: .jpeg Artefacts
description: Five tracks of post, punk leaning into darkwave on .jpeg Artefacts, cut at 45 for the extra weight. Guitars and drum machines doing the usual cold dance, shelve near the gloomier end of the Avant! catalogue.

title: Heaven Up Here
label: Korova
description: Korova revisits the Bunnymen's 1981 record, the one where the group leaned hardest into rhythm section and reverb before the singles took over. Still the moodiest entry in their catalogue.

title: Pilgrimage Of The Dark Friar
label: WereGnome Records
description: Eight tracks of cloistered dungeon synth on WereGnome, the Tennessee label that has quietly become the genre's most reliable address. Candlelit drones and tomb, cold pads, suited to the hour between vespers and sleep.

title: Imago
label: co:clear
description: Nine tracks for co:clear that pull ambient, trip hop and dub into the same low, lit room, with IDM detailing showing up in the seams. Limited pressing; shelve near the slower, headier end of the Modern Love catalogue.

title: Simulated Microcosm
label: Orange Milk Records
description: Seven tracks of plasticky, hyperactive electronics arriving on cassette via Orange Milk, a label that has long made room for music this restless. Sits comfortably alongside the Giant Claw end of the catalog.

title: Secret Love
label: 4AD
description: Eleven tracks of Dry Cleaning's deadpan post, punk for 4AD, with Florence Shaw's spoken non sequiturs presumably still riding the band's coiled, melodic guitar rock. Limited LP for those who keep returning to New Long Leg.

title: World Of Trance 02 (Limited Vinyl Edition)
label: ZYX Music
description: ZYX delivers a 20, track trance compendium curated by Talla 2XLC, the Frankfurt veteran whose name has been synonymous with the genre since the Technoclub era. Limited vinyl pressing for the uplifting, trance faithful.

title: Hongkong
label: Field Records (3)
description: Chain Reaction puts Henke and Behrens' Hongkong back in print, the label's defining statement of humid, location, haunted dub techno still doing the work twenty, some years on. Essential shelving next to Porter Ricks.

title: Defiance
label: Not On Label (Youth Avoiders Self-released)
description: Ten tracks of melodic hardcore from the Parisian punks, pressed at 45 by Destructure in a limited 12". Tight, fast, and unfussy in the way the band's catalogue has always been.

title: Rush On Me EP
label: Lapsus Music
description: Three tracks of trim, peak, time house leaning toward minimal techno, landing on Lapsus in early January. Functional rather than flashy, sized for the room.

title: The Boy And The Tree
label: Lo Recordings
description: Lo Recordings returns to Yokota's pastoral ambient catalogue, twelve pieces of treated acoustics and woozy loops from the late producer's most widely loved register. For anyone shelving Sakura nearby.

title: Confield
label: Beat Records
description: Warp keeps Confield in circulation, the record where Autechre's grids stopped behaving and generative process took over from groove. Still the obvious pivot point between Tri Repetae listeners and whatever they thought they wanted next.

title: Kindred
label: Hyperdub
description: Three tracks of weather, damaged garage and half, collapsed dubstep returned to vinyl by Hyperdub, the Burial template at its most expansive before the ambient drift took over. Essential shelving next to Untrue.

title: Carnival
label: Dais Records
description: Five tracks of Texan shoegaze from Trauma Ray, landing on Dais where the goth and dream, pop wings of the catalog already overlap. Heavier than wistful, but the melodies do the work.

title: Irradiated
label: Appendix.Files
description: Eight tracks of corroded dub techno and ambient drift on Appendix.Files, where the genre's usual gloss gets sanded down to something rougher and more chemical. For anyone whose Deepchord shelf has started leaning toward the noisier end.

title: Street Dogs
label: Hellcat Records
description: Six tracks of Boston street punk on a 45 RPM 10", pressed for Record Store Day on the label that has carried most of the band's catalogue. Built for the Oi! shelf, next to the Cock Sparrer reissues.

title: in filth your mystery is kingdom / far smile peasant in yellow music
label: AD 93
description: Fourteen tracks of warped folk and lo, fi psychedelia from Dagmar Zuniga, landing on AD 93 in a limited LP pressing. Stranger and more song, shaped than the label's club, facing catalogue, closer in spirit to Coby Sey's quieter corners.

title: Feel It All Around
label: Other People Records
description: Eleven tracks of grunge weight pulled through shoegaze haze, the New York band leaning further into their guitar, album instincts for Other People. For anyone whose Hum and Failure records are still in heavy rotation.

title: Period Music
label: Other People
description: Self, titled outing on Nicolas Jaar's Other People, a label that has long preferred records that resist clean genre placement. File alongside the imprint's quieter, more compositional side rather than its dance, floor entries.

title: POMPEII//UTILITY
label: 10K
description: A 33, track double set pairing MIKE with Surf Gang and Earl Sweatshirt on 10K, which is roughly the entire current axis of underground New York rap in one sleeve. Long, sprawling, built to be lived with rather than skimmed.

title: Pompeii/Utility
label: 10K
description: Earl, MIKE and Surf Gang stretch out across 33 tracks for 10K, the kind of sprawl that suggests two records bolted together rather than edited down. Sits where Earl's last few have sat: blunted, conversational, in no hurry to resolve.

title: Not Try
label: Youth Promotion
description: Junior Reid back on his own Youth Promotion imprint for a limited 7", the format the catalogue was built for. Roots singing in its proper home, two sides at 45.

title: Macha Loved Bedhead • Bedhead Loved Macha
label: Numero Group
description: Numero exhumes the brief 2000 collaboration between Athens' gamelan, inflected Macha and the Kadane brothers' Bedhead, six tracks of slowcore drift threaded with field recordings and tuned metal. For anyone whose Bedhead box still gets regular play.

title: See-Through
label: Balmat
description: Twelve pieces of ambient and abstract electronics from the Portland sound artist, landing on Balmat where her field, recording sensibility fits neatly alongside the label's quieter end. For anyone who followed Lichen down the rabbit hole.

title: No Time To Burn
label: Strongly Felt
description: Atlantic dusts off the 1974 Black Heat LP, nine tracks of horn, led DC funk with the loose, gospel, leaning swing that kept the band a crate, digger staple long after the original pressing went scarce. For anyone who wore out the Mr. Bongo reissues.

title: vernacular
label: life is beautiful records
description: Seven tracks from Aloisius on Life Is Beautiful, sitting in the seam between electronic processing, rock instrumentation and modern classical writing. Experimental in the literal sense, less a genre tag than a working method.

title: The World Of Gazzara
label: Irma Records
description: Fifteen tracks of jazz, funk and acid jazz from the long, running Italian producer, landing where you'd expect it to land: Irma, the Bologna label that has been mining this exact seam since the late eighties. For the Montefiori Cocktail crowd.

title: Call Sign Cobra II
label: Snappy Little Numbers
description: Ten tracks of straight, ahead punk rock and roll, remastered and given a limited LP pressing through Snappy Little Numbers. The kind of record that lives or dies on the riff, and seems content with that arrangement.

title: Confield = コンフィールド
label: Warp Records
description: Warp reissues the 2001 record where Autechre fully committed to algorithmic composition, rhythms generated rather than programmed and melody dissolving into structure. Still the album that splits the IDM canon cleanly into before and after.

title: 1977: The Manny Martinez Tapes
label: Really Wasted Youth
description: Thirty, four tracks of 1977, vintage Misfits rehearsals attributed to original drummer Manny Martinez, surfacing as an unofficial limited pressing on Really Wasted Youth. Strictly for collectors already deep into the Glenn Danzig pre, Static Age archaeology.

title: Away
label: Youth Riot
description: Eleven tracks of warped indie rock from the Vancouver outfit, landing on Youth Riot. Guitars still bend at strange angles, songwriting still buried under the noise on purpose.

title: Blessed The Evolution
label: Mind Spray Records
description: Sixteen tracks of unrepentant boom bap from the Gang Starr Foundation veteran, self, released through Mind Spray. Jeru's lane has not moved, and that is the point.

title: Break Down The Walls
label: Revelation Records (8)
description: Wishingwell presses up the 1986 Youth Of Today LP again, twelve tracks of straight edge hardcore that effectively set the template for the late, eighties NYHC stampede. Required shelf alongside Gorilla Biscuits.

title: The North Borders
label: Ninja Tune
description: Ninja Tune press another round of Simon Green's 2013 set, the one where his downtempo widened out into something closer to soul, inflected bass music. Still the cleanest entry point to his catalogue if Black Sands felt too dusk, lit.

title: Virgin Soil
label: Young (5)
description: Two tracks of art rock pressed to a 45 by 1000 Rabbits for Young, format doing some of the framing here. The 7" single as deliberate choice rather than budget call.

title: Space 1.8
label: Warp Records
description: Warp pulls Sinephro's harp and modular debut back into print, eight pieces that sit between spiritual jazz and ambient drift without ever forcing the meeting. For anyone who came in late via Endlessness.

title: Marco Flash - Alex Time - EP Volume 4
label: AUDIO MUSIC WORLD
description: Six tracks of house, deep house, disco and afrobeat threaded through a single 12" on Audio Music World. Functional dancefloor material rather than headphone listening, sequenced for working DJs.

title: Wrap Up A Draw
label: Youth Promotion
description: Junior Reid back on his own Youth Promotion imprint with a two, sider pressed to 7" at 45, the kind of singer, and, version artifact the label has run on for decades. Roots vocal collectors know where to file it.

title: Mijin
label: Leaving Records
description: Ten tracks of beat, craft from the Tokyo producer once known as Bun, landing on Leaving Records. The Hip Hop tag undersells it; expect the kind of hand, built, slightly off, grid instrumentals that sit comfortably alongside Matthewdavid's catalogue.

title: Music For Tombak & Synth
label: Other People
description: Eight pieces from Peyghamy on Nicolas Jaar's Other People, pursuing the tombak and synthesizer dialogue he has been quietly mapping out for a few years now. The frame stays abstract; the hand drumming keeps it grounded.

title: The Campfire Headphase
label: Warp Records
description: Warp keeps the Boards Of Canada catalogue circulating with The Campfire Headphase, the one where the Sandison brothers folded detuned guitar into their tape, warped pastoral. Sits closer to dusk than to the Music Has The Right ecosystem most listeners arrive through.

title: Good Evening We Are Wasted Youth
label: Wasted Youth Records (2)
description: Fourteen tracks of post-punk on the artist's own imprint, pressed in a limited run. Shelve next to the moodier end of the current Iceage / Protomartyr axis.

title: Racional Vol 1
label: Strongly Felt
description: Another pass at the 1975 Racional sessions, the cult Brazilian funk, soul record Maia made while inside the Universo em Desencanto sect. Heavy, sweat, soaked grooves with the strangest lyrical premise in his catalogue; an unofficial LP for the curious.

title: Blue Magic
label: Strongly Felt
description: Atlantic reissues the Philly soul group's self, titled set in a remastered, limited pressing, nine tracks of sweet ballads and lightly disco, tilted R&B from the Norman Harris orbit. For anyone shelving alongside Blue Notes or Delfonics.

title: Middle Man
label: Felt Sense Recordings
description: Five tracks of clipped, glitch, leaning minimal that sit closer to the tech house dancefloor than to laptop abstraction. Felt Sense keeping things lean; for anyone tracking the lineage from Perlon through to the current Sushitech crowd.

title: PK & STRAY
label: Death By Numbers
description: Six tracks of dungeon synth bleeding into hypnagogic indie pop, issued in a limited run by Death By Numbers. The genre tags read like a contradiction; in practice the seam is the point.

title: Marty Supreme (Original Soundtrack)
label: A24 Music
description: Lopatin scoring a Safdie film again, twenty, three cues for A24 Music that lean into the synth register he has spent the last decade refining for screen work. Filed next to the Uncut Gems OST without much argument.

title: Chainsaw Man The Movie: Reze Arc Original Soundtrack -Summer's End-
label: Mappa Records
description: Ushio scoring the Reze arc for Mappa, thirty cues of the same brittle, processed acoustic palette he brought to Devilman Crybaby and A Silent Voice. Score, as, record rather than fan, service; file with his Liminal Spaces work.

title: live at café blue gelato
description: A live document from shinetiac, self, released and tagged only as electronic, which fits the project's habit of putting unrehearsed material out before it has a chance to harden. Treat it as a field recording rather than a finished single.

title: caes
description: New Lucrecia Dalt, arriving without label info attached, which feels of a piece with her recent run of slow, dub, shadowed song forms where rhythm and voice keep slipping past each other. File alongside her RVNG output.

title: Beats In Space 189: Call Super (DJ Mix)
description: Call Super takes the 189th Beats In Space slot, which on past form means a mix that wanders through club registers without ever settling into one lane. File alongside the rest of the BIS guest series.

title: Dancin' In The Streets
label: Modern Love
description: Twelve tracks of ambient and experimental drift from the Manchester producer, landing on Modern Love where the aesthetic fits like a glove. Closer to the label's Andy Stott end of the shelf than the dancefloor the title suggests.

title: Blurrr / Goodness
label: AD 93
description: A split LP on AD 93 pairing Joanne Robertson's haunted folk drift with feeo's quieter electronic sketches across 26 tracks. Sequenced as two halves of the same dim room, for those still playing Blue Car at low volume.

title: Talismann 2
label: Plattenbau Ost
description: Thirteen tracks of German vocal pop from Hagen Stoll on his own Plattenbau Ost imprint, picking up the Talismann thread. Outside the usual remit here, but flagged for completists tracking the label.

title: Short Tracks
label: Short Span
description: Twenty, two miniatures spread across abstract ambient, downtempo and dub techno, the conceit being right there in the label's name. Useful as a sampler if you're auditioning unfamiliar names in the Short Span orbit.

title: Goonator 3000
label: Not On Label
description: Three tracks of pop rap self released as a digital mini, no label apparatus around it. The kind of file, only drop that lives or dies on word of mouth.

title: Studies On A River
label: Good Morning Tapes
description: Four ambient pieces from Omori on Good Morning Tapes, synth work folded into water recordings in the way the label tends to favour. Limited LP; sits comfortably alongside Ulla or Pauline Anna Strom on the shelf.

title: Drames Rurals (Shackleton Mixes)
label: Hivern Discs
description: Shackleton turns his attention to Drames Rurals for Hivern, three reworks that drag the source material into his familiar world of skeletal percussion and dread, tinted dub. For anyone still tracking the Skull Disco lineage.

title: Department
label: INDEX:Records
description: New material on INDEX:Records under the Department alias, the label continuing its run of leftfield club tools that lean closer to texture than function. Worth a look for anyone tracking the imprint's recent output.

title: Cavejaz
label: Leaving Records
description: Thirteen tracks of Brazilian guitar jazz from Fabiano Nascimento, landing on Leaving Records where his quieter bossa leanings have always sat comfortably alongside Carlos Niño's circle. One for the Sam Gendel shelf.

title: Collide
label: AD 93
description: Leif lands on AD 93 with eight tracks that pull his ambient instincts toward something with more drive, krautrock pulse cutting through the long, form drift. Less club, more motorik patience; for those still spinning Loris S. Sarid or the quieter end of the label's roster.

title: Swamp (Ricardo Villalobos Variation)
label: Latency
description: Latency hands a Mortazavi piece to Villalobos, who stretches the Iranian percussionist's tombak figures across his familiar minimal, techno scaffolding. Two takes on the same source, neither in a hurry to resolve.

title: Swamp (Ricardo Villalobos Variation)
label: Latency
description: Villalobos takes Mortazavi's Persian hand, percussion source material and stretches it into the kind of patient, micro, shuffled minimal techno he has been refining for two decades. Latency continuing to put unlikely pairings on wax.

title: Unriliście
label: Nowe Nagrania
description: Thirty, one instrumental hip hop sketches from the veteran Polish beatmaker, sprawling at album length on Nowe Nagrania. The kind of dusted, sample, led work Noon has built a quiet reputation on, presented here without MCs in the way.

title: Wynoś Się Z Mojego Domu
label: Instant Classic
description: Kuba Ziołek's Stara Rzeka project returns to Instant Classic with nine tracks of neofolk pulled toward drone and electronics, the same Polish woodland psychedelia he has been mapping since Cień Chmury Nad Ukrytym Polem. For anyone who keeps that record close.

title: Retox Man
label: Nyege Nyege Tapes
description: Twelve tracks of abstract electronics from Metal Preyers on Nyege Nyege Tapes, the Kampala outpost continuing to host the project's collaged, debris, strewn end of the catalogue. Limited pressing; for anyone tracking Nihiloxica or the wider Hakuna Kulala orbit.

title: Pomegranates
label: Other People
description: Twenty pieces of ambient and experimental work from Jaar on his own Other People, pressed to bioplastic LP. Closer to the long, form, score, adjacent side of his catalogue than the dancefloor one.

title: Late Shift Silk
label: 100% Silk
description: Eleven, track label compilation pulling 100% Silk back into its lane of basement deep house, acid wobble and lo, fi electro. Functional rather than ceremonial, which has always been the Silk way.

title: The Face Of The Earth
label: Ideologic Organ
description: Six pieces of voice and viola from Kenney and Kang, landing on Stephen O'Malley's Ideologic Organ where their Persian classical and free, improv lineage feels entirely at home. Devotional in temperament, not in genre.

title: Come Find Me
description: A loose, after-hours 12" from the Houndstooth regular: woody percussion and half-heard voices sat somewhere between jungle and the more wistful end of Hessle Audio. Contained, not quiet.

title: Because I Told You So
label: Ilian Tape
description: Four tracks of techno on Ilian Tape, which by now is shorthand for a particular kind of swung, broken, step pressure. Shelve next to the Zenker Brothers if you need the family resemblance spelled out.

title: A Replica Screams
label: Ufonic
description: Seven tracks of ambient and experimental electronics from ultrafog on their own Ufonic imprint, pressed as a 12" stereo EP. Closer to the unsettled end of the genre than the consolatory one.

title: The Pavilion Of Dreams
label: Leaving Records
description: Hunter steps further into the spiritual jazz lineage on Leaving Records, a one, sided, etched LP that suits her harp, and, voice register more than any club press could. For listeners shelving Alice Coltrane near Carlos Niño.

title: ...And No One Else Wanted To Play (Deluxe Edition)
label: Trust Records (11)
description: Trust Records gives the 1985 SNFU debut a 42, track deluxe overhaul, expanding one of Canadian hardcore's foundational documents into something closer to a session archive. Skate, punk prehistory, presented as such.

title: Selfless
label: Mood Hut
description: Ten tracks of dub, house and techno on Mood Hut, the Vancouver imprint still drawing the same humid, slightly off, kilter line through dancefloor music it always has. For anyone shelving Pender Street Steppers nearby.

artist: The Beatles = ザ・ビートルズ
title: Free As A Bird / Real Love = フリー・アズ・ア・バード / リアル・ラヴ
label: Apple Records
description: Apple pairs the two mid, 90s Threetles reconstructions on a single Japanese pressing, three decades after they first surfaced as Anthology bait. A collector object more than a listening one, but the Jeff Lynne haze still has its defenders.

title: Jah Nam
label: YUKU
description: Eight tracks from Muskila on YUKU, splicing dub techno's chamber pressure with the skitter of footwork and juke. An odd hybrid on paper that the label has been quietly building a case for.

title: Anomaly Index
label: Nyege Nyege Tapes
description: Two pieces from Nkisi for Nyege Nyege Tapes, pairing field recordings with the kind of percussive noise her Initiation discs sharpened into a method. Less club, facing than her earlier work; closer to ritual document.

title: Free As A Bird / Real Love
label: Apple Records
description: Apple reissues the two mid, 90s Threetles reconstructions as a limited 7", thirty years on from the Anthology rollout. Catalogue housekeeping more than revelation, but the format finally suits the songs.

title: Córdoba #GU48 (Collector's Edition)
label: Global Underground (3)
description: Guy J takes the GU mix, series chair for the Córdoba edition, 46 tracks pulled across progressive house, breaks and downtempo into the long, arc shape Global Underground built its name on. Deluxe pressing for the people who still buy these as objects.

title: Leijonaa Metsästän
label: Roihis Musica
description: Twelve tracks of Finnish conscious rap from Asa, reissued on Roihis Musica. The kind of record where the writing carries the weight; shelve near Paleface if you want a domestic reference point.

title: Forever, I've Been Being Born
label: Ideologic Organ
description: Jesse Sykes returns to Southern Lord with ten songs of weathered, slow, burning folk rock, the kind of songwriting where the room around the voice does as much work as the voice itself. Limited LP pressing tied to Record Store Day.

title: Garden On The Palm
label: R & S Records
description: Ken Ishii's R&S, era headtrip gets another pressing, seven tracks of the angular, slightly alien Tokyo techno that put him on the label's map in the first place. Sits comfortably next to Beaumont Hannant if you're filing chronologically.

title: Sleeping Madness
label: R & S Records
description: Ken Ishii back on R&S in reissue form, eleven tracks spanning the techno, breaks and house registers he was already braiding together in the mid, 90s. A useful one if your Jelly Tones is wearing thin.

title: Innerelements
label: R & S Records
description: R&S returns to Ishii's mid, 90s catalogue with a thirteen, track set straddling techno, minimal and the more abstract corners of his work. A useful entry point if you only know him through Jelly Tones.

title: Rain & Cymbals
label: 12th Isle
description: A split LP on 12th Isle pairing Material Things and Pike across six tracks that drift between Berlin, school patience, dub weight and concrète clutter. Sits comfortably with the rest of the Glasgow label's catalogue.

artist: Kali Malone + Drew McDowall = カリ・マローン* アンド ドリュー・マクドウォルー
title: Magnetism = マグネティズム
label: Ideologic Organ
description: Malone and McDowall meet on Stephen O'Malley's Ideologic Organ for five pieces of slow electroacoustic drone, organ minimalism brushing against modular weight. Sits comfortably alongside her own Living Torch.

title: Changes In Air
label: Smalltown Supersound
description: Coverdale on Smalltown Supersound, five pieces of organ, haunted ambient and modern classical that keep the slow harmonic drift of her earlier work intact. Sits comfortably next to Sarah Davachi if you're shelving by mood.

title: Tranquilizer
label: Warp Records
description: Lopatin dials back the maximalism. Warp-issued, structurally loose, more interested in the texture of a decaying sample than the payoff. For anyone who prefers Replica to Garden of Delete.

title: Cavejaz
label: Leaving Records
description: Thirteen tracks of Brazilian guitar work from Fabiano Do Nascimento, landing on Leaving Records and leaning into the bossa lineage rather than away from it. For anyone shelving Arthur Verocai near Matthewdavid's more pastoral output.

title: Jelly Tones
label: R & S Records
description: R & S brings back the 1995 Ishii album that paired Detroit, leaning techno with the cartoon melodicism of his Tokyo studio years. Still the obvious entry point if you came to him via Extra.

title: I Don't Care EP
label: Lapsus Music
description: Two tracks of minimal techno from Hotinga on Lapsus, the Barcelona label that has long favored the drier, more functional end of the style. Tool music for the back half of the night.

title: Deformity In Ceremony
label: Lilang Isla
description: Twelve tracks of dense, riff, forward death metal from Sallow Moth, pressed as a limited EP on Lilang Isla. Closer to the project's solo, demo, feel lineage than to anything polished for the pit.

title: Anthology 4
label: Apple Records
description: A fourth Anthology volume from the Beatles, gathering 36 outtakes, demos and alternate passes across the catalogue for Apple. Strictly for the deep, shelf collectors who have already worn through the 1995, 96 set.

title: Infinity Gradient
label: Erased Tapes Records
description: Perich's 1, bit electronics paired with James McVinnie's organ across eight pieces for Erased Tapes, the math, rigid pulse rubbing against pipework that breathes. Sits comfortably next to Nils Frahm's more austere keyboard work on the label.

title: Blue Permutations
label: Lilang Isla
description: Four tracks of death metal from Sallow Moth, the solo project's catalogue continues on Lilang Isla in a limited EP pressing. For listeners tracking the more compositional, riff, dense end of the underground.

title: Allergic
label: NAFF
description: Two tracks from B. McQueen and Priori on NAFF, sitting in the gap between dub techno's drift and dubstep's weight without committing to either. A 10" at 45, which suits the format: short, dense, room for low end.

title: Amami (feat. Minami Kizuki)
description: Yussef Dayes pairs with Japanese folk singer Minami Kizuki on a single that should, on paper, sit some distance from the drummer's South London jazz orbit. Worth a listen for anyone tracking where his collaborations keep wandering.

title: Death Folk
label: Bamboo Shows
description: Six tracks pitched between alternative rock, folk metal and doom on Bamboo Shows, less a pastiche than a working, out of where those three modes share a tempo. Heavy without theatrics.

title: Eastside Hardcore Vol. I (An Eastern European Sampler)
label: Frabylon
description: Eight, band hardcore sampler from Frabylon mapping the current Eastern European scene, pressed in limited quantity. A scene document more than a curated mixtape, useful if you have been tracking the region past the obvious Czech and Polish names.

title: sorry i thought you were someone else
label: Incienso
description: K, Lone lands on Incienso with ten tracks of minimal, garage, inflected house that keeps the Wisdom Teeth lightness intact while sitting comfortably in the label's downtown lineage. Reference point: Anthony Naples in his most dancefloor, leaning mode.

title: Airdrop III
label: Peak Oil
description: Low End Activist lands on Peak Oil with ten tracks pulling UK garage into the rougher, more abstract terrain the label tends to favour. Sound system music for people who own Beneath records.

title: Osaka Cuts
label: Coastline Northern Cuts
description: A three, track 7" from the Polish Coastline Northern Cuts crew, splitting the difference between hip hop, jazz and R&B in the kind of short, looped sketches the label has built its catalogue on. Cut at both 33 and 45, so flip accordingly.

title: Bemenet / Kimenet
label: Coastline Northern Cuts
description: Seven tracks from Tenemik on Coastline Northern Cuts, pulling dub techno toward krautrock's longer arcs without ever quite settling in either camp. Patient, abstract, more rhythm, as, drift than rhythm, as, grid.

title: Airdrop II
label: Peak Oil
description: Low End Activist lands on Peak Oil with ten tracks moving between bass weight, drum and bass pressure and grainier experimental terrain. A natural fit for anyone tracking Pessimist's recent output.

title: Vesper Sparrow
label: Shelter Press
description: Six pieces from JJJJJerome Ellis on Shelter Press, threading spoken word through free improvisation and concrète textures in the way the label has long made room for. Sits comfortably alongside Moor Mother on the shelf.

title: Wipe'out'' - The Zero Gravity Soundtrack Vol. 2
label: Lapsus Records
description: Lapsus continues its archival work on Tim Wright's Wipeout scores, gathering 22 tracks across the drum and bass, electro and trance vocabulary that PlayStation, era racing burned into a generation. Remastered, on LP, for those who treat game soundtracks as a serious shelf.

title: Big Mama EP
label: Lapsus Music
description: Two, tracker of straight, ahead house from Fiorella on Lapsus, the Barcelona label that tends to favour the cleaner, club, functional end of the spectrum. Built for the floor rather than the headphones.

title: II = II
label: Modern Love
description: Four pieces of experimental drone for Modern Love, Sara Udon working in the smudged, low, light register the label has spent two decades shaping. Sits comfortably alongside Rainer Veil for anyone tracking that lineage.

title: A Body Like A Home
label: Other People
description: Thirteen pieces from Alejandra Cárdenas on Nicolas Jaar's Other People, drawing field recording, sound poetry, drone and cumbia into the same room without smoothing the edges between them. Voice and document treated as instruments; shelve near Lara Sarkissian.

title: Illusion
label: Ilian Tape
description: Four, track 12" from the Munich brothers on their own Ilian Tape, working the broken, dust, flecked techno register the label has spent a decade defining. For anyone tracking the Skee Mask adjacent end of the catalogue.

title: Magnetism
label: Ideologic Organ
description: Malone and McDowall convene on Stephen O'Malley's Ideologic Organ for five pieces of slow, moving drone and electroacoustic minimalism, the kind of patient harmonic work both have built careers around. Sits comfortably next to the Coil, adjacent end of the label.

title: Mille Risposte (Dopplereffekt Isotopic Filter Re Structure)
label: Latency
description: Dopplereffekt put their isotopic electro grid under Tarta Relena's Catalan vocal duo, and the result sits closer to Drexciyan radio static than to anything you'd file under folk. Latency in matchmaker mode.

title: Now I Know What Dreams Are Made Of
label: Unseelie
description: Thirteen tracks of sugar, rushed hyperpop from HIMERA on Unseelie, where dance, pop hooks get pulled apart and reassembled at double speed. Sits comfortably alongside the Quannnic crowd if you need a shelving cue.

title: 84 Days
label: Double Helix Records (2)
description: Eleven tracks of straight, ahead punk on Double Helix, pressed in a limited LP run. No frills in the framing and probably none in the playing either.

title: Manzana
label: Balmat
description: Mike Paradinas lands on Balmat with thirteen tracks that wander through his familiar IDM, breakbeat and ambient territories without settling in any of them. Less a statement than a notebook, which suits the label.

title: Toso Toso
label: Leaving Records
description: Seven tracks of avant, jazz, glitch and pop pulled into the same room, arriving on Leaving in a limited LP pressing. Sits comfortably near the more song, shaped end of the label's catalogue, think Carlos Niño's wider orbit.

title: Minecraft Volume Alpha
label: Ghostly International
description: Ghostly reissues the soundtrack that scored a generation's idle building sessions, twenty, four pieces of plainspoken piano and soft, edged synth ambient from Daniel Rosenfeld. The music has long since outgrown the game.

title: The Unavoidable EP
label: A Sky Full Of Numbers
description: Four tracks from Winkles for A Sky Full Of Numbers, splitting the difference between techno propulsion and ambient drift, pressed to bioplastic 12". Functional and reflective in roughly equal measure.

title: Songs for Nothing
label: AD 93
description: Olan Monk pushes further into smeared dream pop territory on AD 93, with shoegaze drift colliding against something distinctly Celtic at the edges. Ten tracks that sit closer to song-form than the label's usual club remit.

title: Sharp Fragments
label: Ilian Tape
description: Ilian Tape's Stenny commits to the harder end of the label's Munich palette: swung hi-hats, tunnelling sub, the odd passage of near-breakcore. Tools, not tracks.

title: FILE 2
description: A second installment in the H.LLS FILE series, filed under alternative without much else by way of signposting. Self, released and brief, the kind of drop that asks you to take it on its own terms.

title: Simulacra
label: Mood Hut
description: Nine tracks of slow, moving downtempo and ambient with a tribal pulse, Slow Riffs landing on Mood Hut where that kind of unhurried, vaguely sun, warmed atmosphere has long been house style. For anyone who follows the Pender Street Steppers end of the catalogue.

title: Phantom Keys
label: Nyege Nyege Tapes
description: Four tracks pairing the Busoga embaire xylophone troupe with Naoyuki Uchida's dub processing, exactly the kind of cross, wired meeting Nyege Nyege has built its catalogue on. The wood resonates, the delays do the rest.

title: Big city life EDITS
label: Escho
description: Smerz return to Escho with a fourteen, track edits set, the Norwegian duo's askew take on pop reworked into something looser and more club, leaning. For anyone who keeps revisiting Believer.

title: The Lighthouse
label: Not On Label (Social Youth Cult Self-released)
description: Self, released goth rock from Social Youth Cult, eight tracks of the genre's familiar furniture: chorused bass, declamatory vocals, the long shadow of the Sisters and early 4AD. For listeners still mining that seam.

title: Foundry / Bonita
label: Short Span
description: Yu Su steps toward the dancefloor on Short Span, a two-tracker that swaps her usual dubby drift for acid-flecked tech house and techno cut at 45. For anyone who clocked the harder edges in her DJ sets.

label: Peak Oil
description: Peak Oil reissues the Lifted collective's third, a record of slow-moving ambient jazz where the playing feels suspended rather than performed. Reference point if needed: the more horizontal corners of the Music From Memory catalogue.

title: #einaufden 1
label: Plattenbau Ost
description: Sixteen spoken-word tracks on CDr from Plattenbau Ost, filed under audiobook rather than music. One for the German-language shelf, not the listening chair.

title: Holy Cross Blues
label: Not On Label (The Deslondes Self-released)
description: Self-released country, folk and gospel from The Tumbleweeds, twelve tracks pressed to LP without label backing. Porch-music territory rather than revivalist costume; for anyone who follows the Deslondes orbit.

title: The Scottish Four Seasons
label: Not On Label (Isla Ratcliff self-released)
description: Self-released folk from Scottish fiddler Isla Ratcliff, fourteen tracks structured around the seasonal frame the title makes plain. Trad-leaning rather than crossover, shelve with Aidan O'Rourke or Lauren MacColl.

title: Subterra
label: INDEX:Records
description: Eight tracks of bass-weighted alt-pop from Beau Mahadev for INDEX:Records, where deconstructed club textures keep colliding with something closer to a song. For listeners tracking the IDM-pop overlap that LOFT and Iceboy Violet have been working through.

title: Barbaric Nature
label: Youth Attack
description: Twenty tracks of Cadaver Dog hardcore reissued through Mark McCoy's Youth Attack, a label that has long defined a particular strain of ugly, blown-out American HC. Limited LP, shelve next to Gas Chamber.

title: Summertimes Blues (The First Singles & More)
label: Pan-Am Records
description: A Pan-Am compilation gathering early Beach Boys singles era material across fifteen tracks on a single 12". Strictly for the surf-and-harmony shelf, archival rather than essential.

title: Fog
label: Short Span
description: Seven tracks of low-lit downtempo for Short Span, sliding between ambient drift, dub weight and the looser end of bass music. Plays best at 2am, when the genre tags stop mattering.

artist: John & Yoko*, The Plastic Ono Band With The Harlem Community Choir
title: Happy Xmas (War Is Over)
label: Apple Records
description: Apple revisits the 1971 Lennon/Ono Christmas single on a 7", Harlem Community Choir intact. A protest song that long ago slipped into the seasonal canon, returned to its original format.

label: Balmat
description: Mike Paradinas turns toward long-form ambient for Balmat, fifteen pieces that trade the braindance fidget for something patient and pastel. Sits comfortably next to the label's Purelink output without sounding like anyone but him.

title: The Death Of Music
label: Orange Milk Records
description: Ten tracks of deconstructed club for Orange Milk, the label still doing more than anyone to map the seam between maximalist net-music and the dancefloor. Sits comfortably next to the Lillerne and Quantum Natives end of that conversation.

title: Now And Never
label: Isla
description: Eight tracks of cumbia slowed into ambient dub on Isla, the New York label that has made this particular crossing its house style. For anyone who keeps returning to DJ Python.

title: Interception
label: International Chrome
description: Ten tracks of high-impact electro and ghettotech from the International Chrome boss, the kind of muscular, peak-time material the label has built its catalogue around. Closer to DJ Stingray than to anything contemplative.

title: Fly In Amber
label: NAFF
description: Five tracks of ambient and dub techno from Cousin and Priori, paired up on NAFF for a 12". Shelve near Topdown Dialectic if the slow-decay, dub-adjacent end of the spectrum is where you tend to land.

title: Is this a queue
label: AD 93
description: Alpha Maid lands on AD 93 with nine tracks of guitar-noise and electronics that refuse to settle into either rock or club shapes. The label's appetite for awkward, in-between records continues to pay off.

title: Unruly Sun
label: Twin System
description: Two tracks from Floor Length Skirts on Twin System, sitting at the soul-leaning edge of trip hop with downtempo and Latin inflections threaded through. Issued as a limited mixtape object rather than a conventional single.

title: QQ (Second Edition)
label: Isla To Isla
description: Isla To Isla bring back punktò's QQ in a second edition, eight tracks of electroclash sitting close enough to synth-pop that the seams show. For anyone whose shelf already runs from Miss Kittin toward the brattier end of Italians Do It Better.

title: Exinfinite
label: Pan (3)
description: Nine tracks of industrial drone and post-rock erosion from Venera, landing on PAN where the electroacoustic and the corroded sit comfortably together. For listeners who file Emptyset and Puce Mary on the same shelf.

artist: Sun Ra And His Myth-Science Arkestra
title: Fate In A Pleasant Mood
label: Pan-Am Records
description: A reissue of one of Sun Ra's early-60s Saturn sides, where the Arkestra is still leaning more swing than cosmic abstraction. Shelve next to Angels and Demons at Play if you need a pointer.

title: Teal Dreams
label: AMF Records (3)
description: Yazmin Lacey settles into a fourteen-track LP for AMF, the kind of unhurried neo-soul writing she has been quietly building a name on. For anyone who keeps Cleo Sol close to the turntable.

title: Right Here, Right Now
label: Long Branch Records
description: Nine tracks of measured, melodic prog from Our Oceans, the kind of patient, jazz-inflected writing Long Branch has been quietly cataloguing for years. Closer in temperament to latter-day Cynic than to anything overtly heavy.

title: Achlys
label: Shelter Press
description: Eight pieces of slow, attenuated ambient from the Barn Owl half on Shelter Press, where minimalism tends to mean room tone and patience rather than melodic relief. For anyone tracking the label's quieter Sarah Davachi end.

title: Love Me! EP
label: Lapsus Music
description: Two cuts of trim, functional minimal techno from Bizza, landing on Lapsus in their usual digital-EP format. Built for the floor rather than the headphones, with the restraint the label tends to favor.

title: I Trust Pain
label: Fixed Abode
description: Eleven tracks of Culver's bleak spoken-word electronics, this time pulled toward drill's grey weight rather than industrial abstraction. Limited 12" on his own Fixed Abode, and still recognisably the same voice muttering over the rubble.

title: Live Laugh Love
label: Warner Records
description: Eleven tracks of Earl in his familiar register: low-stakes drums, dust on the loops, verses delivered like he's the only one in the room. Warner pressing it to vinyl, which still feels slightly incongruous for music this interior.

title: We're Here All The Time
label: Theory Therapy
description: Seven tracks of fractured breaks and ambient drift on Theory Therapy, sitting where IDM's nervous edits meet a softer, hazier middle distance. For listeners who still pull out Lone or early Bibio when the mood calls for it.

title: Don't Trust The Government
label: Double Helix Records (2)
description: Three tracks of plain-spoken punk from 84 Days on Double Helix, the title doing most of the rhetorical work before a note plays. Functional, unfussy, exactly what the sleeve advertises.

title: Golden Microphone From Rainy Sicily
label: Muscut
description: Ten pieces of ambient dub and tape experiment from the Ukrainian sound artist, reissued on Kyiv's Muscut in a limited pressing. Shelve near Andrew Pekler if you need a pointer.

title: In Transit
label: FELT (3)
description: Six pieces of ambient on FELT, an outfit whose catalogue tends toward the patient and unhurried. Filed under project-name-as-album-title, which suits the contents.

title: The Spectral Citadel
label: Ilian Tape
description: Four tracks of techno on Ilian Tape, a label whose Munich house style has long favoured rugged drum programming over rigid grids. Sits comfortably alongside the Zenker Brothers end of the catalogue.

title: Rhythm Immortal
label: Modern Love
description: Eight tracks of percussive abstraction from Carrier on Modern Love, cut at 45 for the kind of detail the label tends to favor. Sits comfortably alongside Rainy Miller or Space Afrika on the shelf.

title: Petty Relics
label: Black Numbers
description: Eleven tracks of melodic punk from the Jersey lifers, landing on Black Numbers where their post-hardcore edges still get room to bruise the choruses. For anyone whose shelf already holds The Menzingers and Iron Chic.

title: Nexus
label: Latency
description: Mortazavi's tombak and daf work continues to translate cleanly into electronic terms, here across nine pieces for Latency. The label suits him: percussion treated less as rhythm than as a tunable surface.

title: Classics
label: R & S Records
description: R & S brings the early Aphex compendium back to vinyl, remastered, gathering the rave-adjacent hardcore and bleep work that sat alongside the more contemplative SAW material. Useful context for anyone who only knows the later catalogue.

title: Meet The Family
label: SBÄM Records
description: Long-running Sydney punks back in print via Austria's SBÄM, eighteen tracks of the fast, sour, deeply unserious melodic punk they've made their trade for three decades. For the NOFX shelf, no apologies.

title: Mov. Amplio
label: Isla Visión
description: Ten tracks of electroacoustic abstraction from El Piyi on Isla Visión, the Spanish imprint that's quietly become a reliable home for this kind of patient, processed listening. More room-tone than rhythm; shelve near the experimental end of the catalogue.

title: These Exact Days, These Peaceful Nights
label: Snappy Little Numbers
description: Twelve songs from the Edmonton songwriter for Denver's Snappy Little Numbers, sitting where acoustic folk rock meets the label's punk lineage. For anyone whose shelf already runs from Tim Barry to Chris Farren.

title: Broken Glass Arch
label: R & S Records
description: Five tracks of Djrum's signature breadth, ambient drift sharing a sleeve with techno proper, repressed on R & S. For anyone who wore out Portrait With Firewood.

title: Fumarola
label: mappa
description: Eight pieces of slow, abstract drone from Kult Masek and Petr Vrba on Slovakia's mappa, the kind of patient acoustic-electronic smear the label has built its catalogue around. For anyone who keeps returning to Jonáš Gruska's own outings.

title: Beyond Knowhere
label: Good Morning Tapes
description: Three tracks of acid-laced Goa trance on Good Morning Tapes, a label more often associated with horizontal ambient than 303 workouts. The pairing is the interesting part; file alongside the recent Khotin if you want a softer landing strip nearby.

title: Goodness
label: AD 93
description: Eleven tracks of vocal-led ambient and experimental electronics from feeo on AD 93, the label continuing its quiet run of releases that sit between song-form and texture. For anyone tracking Coby Sey's corner of the catalogue.

title: Don’t Look For Answers
label: AMF Records (3)
description: Nine tracks of guitar-forward indie rock from Arkayla, pressed as a limited 12" on AMF. Shelve with the contemporary end of the genre rather than its revivalist wing.

title: Aura Reworks
label: Erased Tapes Records
description: Erased Tapes hands the Hatis Noit songbook over for reworking, her solo-vocal source material pulled into the ambient and experimental orbit the label tends to occupy. For listeners who keep returning to Aura rather than moving on from it.

title: Through Friendly Waters
label: Lapsus Records
description: Lapsus pulls a Kettel album back into print on remastered vinyl, eleven tracks of the melodic, sentimental IDM the Dutch producer has worked in for two decades. For anyone whose Rephlex shelf is missing a softer counterpoint.

title: Through Friendly Waters (20th Anniversary Edition)
label: Lapsus Records
description: Lapsus reissues Kettel's 2005 album of melodic, music-box IDM, remastered across eleven tracks. Still one of the warmer documents from that Sending Orbs/Rephlex axis, for anyone whose Bibio shelf could use deepening.

title: Wait A Minute
label: Lapsus Music
description: Two cuts of unfussy minimal techno from Mattia Red on Lapsus Music, the Barcelona label still mining the dry, functional end of the genre. Tool music for the second room.

title: Humming Fuzz
label: Knekelhuis
description: Seven tracks for Knekelhuis that sit awkwardly across acid rock, krautrock motorik and slow house, which is roughly where the label has been digging lately. Less a fusion than a shrug between rooms; for anyone who got on with the recent Lifted-adjacent end of the catalogue.

title: Configuration Support
label: Ilian Tape
description: Four tracks of Dario Zenker on the family label, which is to say bruised, off-grid techno cut with the broken-beat looseness Ilian Tape has made its house style. Sits comfortably next to anything Skee Mask has filed under the same logo.

title: Rest Here
label: NAFF
description: Twelve tracks of neofolk-leaning downtempo from Car Culture on NAFF, where acoustic textures sit comfortably alongside the label's usual leftfield electronic bent. Pressed to LP for those who like their pastoral music a little smudged.

title: Puente Del Mundo
label: Son de Isla Verde
description: Self-released salsa from Son de Isla Verde, a single arriving without much fanfare and squarely in the traditional brass-and-clave register rather than any crossover lane. One for the salsa dura shelf.

title: Nocturnal Rainforest
label: Pan (3)
description: Three-way summit on PAN: Masami Akita's noise grain, Cavalera's percussive instinct, and Bernocchi's dark-ambient long-form thinking, condensed into two pieces. Drone and abrasion treated as the same material.

title: Don't Care. Didn't Ask.
label: Snappy Little Numbers
description: Eleven tracks of Colorado punk on Snappy Little Numbers, where Cheap Perfume continue trading in the kind of plainspoken, politically pissed-off hooks that don't need decoding. Shelve near Mannequin Pussy if you need a pointer.

title: Mahal
label: Ninja Tune
description: The masked Melbourne trio's Ninja Tune EP gets a repress, five tracks of looping eastern-tinged guitar figures and live-band funk that sit closer to library psych than to anything currently passing for fusion. For the Khruangbin shelf, but tighter wound.

title: Sun Archive
label: 100% Silk
description: Akasha System returns to 100% Silk for an eight-track downtempo set on cassette, holding to the sort of melodic, sun-faded electronics the label has long traded in. For anyone still reaching for Octo Octa's quieter detours.

title: Houzz 14
label: Balmat
description: Mike Paradinas drops a one-tracker on Balmat, a label more often associated with placid ambient than IDM brain-knots. Worth hearing what happens when a Planet Mu lifer turns up at that address.

title: The Creep
label: Ideologic Organ
description: Ideologic Organ reissues Slomo's long-form drone behemoth on a limited LP, two tracks of slow-burning doom-ambient that sit closer to a tectonic shift than a song. For anyone whose Sunn O))) shelf has room for the more meditative end.

title: Xylem Tube EP
label: R & S Records
description: R & S returns to the early Richard D. James catalogue, six tracks of acid-spiked breakbeat techno from the period when his vocabulary was still being assembled in real time. Remastered 12", for anyone whose Analogue Bubblebath copies are getting tired.

title: Pohreb
label: mappa
description: Thirteen pieces of field recording, drone and ambient assembled for mappa, the Slovak imprint that treats documentary sound and composition as the same gesture. Sits comfortably alongside Jonáš Gruska's own catalogue work.

title: Jon Savage's 1986-1990 (Rollin' Under The Melody)
label: Ace
description: The writer-curator's late-80s sweep for Ace, 32 tracks pulling indie rock, early house and hip hop into one frame as it was actually heard at the time. More cultural diary than genre exercise.

title: Meanwhile...On The Outside
label: Death By Numbers
description: Four tracks of hypnagogic pop drift from Jeebus on Death By Numbers, sitting where bedroom new age leaks into something closer to indie songwriting. For listeners who keep going back to the softer corners of the 100% Silk catalog.

title: Behind Closed Doors/The Shadow Beneath...
label: Death By Numbers
description: Eight tracks of bossa, easy listening and indie pop filed under electronic, which tells you most of what you need about the angle Death By Numbers is taking here. Lounge moves rerouted through a producer's ear rather than a crate-digger's.

title: Find Your Way Back Home
label: Double Helix Records (2)
description: Two-track punk single from 84 Days on Double Helix, digital only. Short, direct, no frills attached.

title: No Scope
label: Ghostly International
description: Twelve tracks of hazed, guitar-leaning dream pop from Crushed, landing on Ghostly. The Britpop scaffolding under the gauze gives it more spine than the genre usually allows; try it next to Jane Remover's softer turns.

title: Certain Things You Can't Explain (I'll Just Let Myself Go)
label: Brainfeeder
description: Kit Sebastian on Brainfeeder continues to make sense the more you sit with it: Anatolian psych filtered through bossa drift and lounge jazz, with none of the dust-fetish that usually attends the formula. A single, but it carries weight.

title: Iris Out / Jane Doe
label: Reissue Records
description: Two Kenshi Yonezu A-sides bundled for Reissue Records, the kind of widescreen J-pop/J-rock hybrid he has built a career on, here tied to anime theme duty. For listeners who already follow the Chainsaw Man pipeline.

title: Reverse Acceleration Of Dragons
label: 12th Isle
description: Five pieces of abstract ambient and drone from Radx, landing on 12th Isle in the becalmed, slightly off-map register the Glasgow label has made its own. Closer to weather than composition.

title: Comafields / Imaginary Festival
label: Hyperdub
description: Two more long-form pieces from Bevan on Hyperdub, sitting in the smeared ambient-bass register he has occupied for years now rather than the garage rhythms he came in on. For the faithful; no one else is making records quite like these.

title: Blurrr
label: AD 93
description: Robertson's hushed, smeared folk lands on AD 93, an unlikely but increasingly logical home for her guitar sketches and ghosted vocals. Nine tracks that sound less written than left out in the weather.

title: The Aftermath
label: Death By Numbers
description: Eight tracks of power violence and thrash compressed into mini-album length on Death By Numbers, the limited pressing suiting the format. Short, blunt, no interest in stretching anything out.

title: Silent Green
label: Cirrus (4)
description: Four tracks of slow, weighted ambient and downtempo from OK EG on Cirrus, the kind of record that sits with the curtains half-drawn. Pair it with the more interior corners of the Music From Memory orbit.

title: ASC - EP1
label: A Strange Child
description: Four techno cuts on A Strange Child, a label that has been quietly building a roster around stripped, club-functional 12"s. Cut across 33 and 45rpm, which usually signals an A-side built for the floor and a B-side that wanders.

title: Found Songs
label: Erased Tapes Records
description: Erased Tapes reissues the 2009 piano-and-strings sketches that first marked out Arnalds' lane in modern classical, remastered and pressed to a pair of 45rpm 10"s. Slight, unhurried, and still the clearest entry point to everything he made after.

title: II
label: Sferic
description: Nineteen tracks of cloud rap and trap dissolved into the kind of weather-system ambient Sferic usually presses to clear vinyl. An odd fit for the label on paper, but the smudged edges make sense once you're in it.

title: Shifted
label: Short Span
description: Three tracks of dub techno from Conna Haraway on Short Span, pressed as a 12" EP at 33⅓. Chord stabs and tape hiss in the lineage you'd expect; file near Yagya if you need a shelf.
